posts.text: He's trying to run, but Congress should not let him hide. Calley Means worked the laws from the inside to benefit his own company, making millions of dollars. https://t.co/63z0LHImhH
So you’re funding the Russian war against Ukraine because you *started* a losing war in Iran. https://t.co/T9p1cuMN2r

Eliya Cohen was held hostage in Hamas' terror tunnels for 505 days. He was chained, starved, and beaten. Every morning, he and his fellow captives prayed in Hebrew so that their captors would know that their Jewish spirit was unbroken. His girlfriend, Ziv Abud, was with him at the Nova Music Festival. She escaped a bomb shelter in which their family and friends were murdered by terrorists using grenades & guns. 

Eliya & Ziv were honored guests at Temple Shalom in Newton on October 7th to share their story (he learned English from a book that Hersh Goldberg-Polin gave him to pass the time in the tunnels) in commemoration of the third anniversary of the Hamas attacks. I joined hundreds of others to bear witness, memorialize the thousands slain, and take inspiration from the indomitable spirit of Eliya and Ziv. Sustaining Americans' memory of October 7th is an homage for the victims, a tribute to the heroes, and a powerful way to strengthen the resolve of the Jewish community.

A new treatment that slows Alzheimer's progression could generate more than $100,000 in lifetime social value per person. Even more if started earlier. My bipartisan Alzheimer's Early Detection Act would give every American that early start by covering biomarker testing, which is good medicine and smart money. Pre-symptomatic individuals shouldn't need to wait to show symptoms to start the treatment that can delay the decline.

Most immigrants detained have no criminal record. The mass arrests in Fall River & New Bedford are not supporting public safety; they are an attempt by the president to distract from diesel at $6.50/gallon. https://t.co/8ufpH55ZWe

Stripping $300,000 from the Massachusetts Immigrant and Refugee Advocacy Coalition (MIRA) is performative cruelty in line with this administration’s lengthy track record of harassing and intimidating immigrant communities. 

It is also a direct violation of the law. The Constitution gives Congress, not Russell Vought, sole authority over federal spending. Lawmakers must reassert our Article I power of the purse, stop these illegal impoundments, and roll back this imperial presidency.

https://t.co/jGWBbRe118

The ICE arrest wave in the South Coast is sowing fear in the immigrant communities I represent. This broken agency continues to undermine public safety, which requires trust, due process, and professional law enforcement. ICE must provide a rationale & update for each individual arrested in this operation, and my office is ready to assist constituents. Congress should pass the Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act, which I have co-sponsored.

https://t.co/I2PHlbibjZ

Vought is increasingly isolated on medical science funding - on Appropriations, Uniform Grants Regulation, and the EO, he has been beaten back. Merit-based science backers need to go on offense, now: the forward funding & grant freezes at NIH need to stop, too. https://t.co/7kiJsCbL8E

Project 2025 architect Russell Vought views medical science as a blue-state subsidy, not a public good. Vought's OMB is waging a multi-front war against the NIH's funding and peer review. Red-state researchers: time to launch a counter-attack. Tell your representatives & senators to keep politics out of the scientific method.

AI regulation starts with AI liability. My bipartisan Deepfake Liability Act holds AI accountable to the common sense and wisdom embedded in common law by everyday people. Ignore the naysayers who claim that only tech experts can regulate tech; for hundreds of years, liability has been an effective tool for society to promote innovation while insisting upon responsibility.

Today I voted to pass tough Russia sanctions legislation in the House. It has already passed the Senate, 86-11, and will now be signed into law. The law will impose tariffs on the top importers of Russian oil.

I voted Yes because this legislation is critical to the support and defense of Ukraine as it fights on the front lines of the free world. Appeasement does not work. Victory is vital. 

To achieve a victory in which Ukraine's eastern border is secure; it can transport goods through the Black Sea; and it joins the European Union; NATO and partner nations must sanction Russian oil & gas exports while authorizing & equipping our ally to strike Russian oil & gas infrastructure directly. Only sanctions and strikes can strangle Vladimir Putin's war economy, for which oil is the lifeblood. 

Concerns have been raised that this legislation empowers the president's expensive and chaotic trade policy. This legislation does not create broad, unilateral tariff authority or give the President a new general-purpose trade weapon. It is Congress finally exercising its Article I authority to direct targeted tariffs at countries providing material support for Russia’s war against Ukraine. The Trump Administration’s damaging national security and trade strategy underscores the importance of Congress reasserting itself as a constitutional check on the President’s authority.
Australia’s approach is working and America should fast follow. https://t.co/YiIfEoJ5yx

I was honored to deliver the keynote remarks at Taunton’s commemoration of the 25th anniversary of September 11. Below are my remarks:

“It’s an honor to address this solemn assembly as we commemorate the 25th anniversary of the attacks on September 11. That day is increasingly used as a marker – a pivot point – for what came before and what came after. It ended the innocent 1990s sense of one global village that had taken hold since the fall of the Soviet Union. It launched a series of wars whose seismic shocks are still shaking the Middle East today.

Yet we owe it to the victims and heroes who experienced that day – and to my children’s generation who did not – to memorialize September 11 unto itself. Not for what came before. Not for what came after. But for the blood, sweat and tears of that awful event itself.

It was a day of unbearable tragedy. Office workers jumped from skyscrapers rather rather than burn in an inferno. Airplane passengers lurched to collision in terrifying final moments. 

It was a day of remarkable heroism. Police officers and firefighters ran into those skyscrapers, into those infernos; many did not return. Airplane passengers stormed the cockpit, so that the final, terrifying collision did not kill other innocents. 

And it was a day of solidarity. Ferry boat pilots flocked to southern Manhattan to shepherd hundreds of thousands of New Yorkers to safety. Allied leaders pledged support and mutual defense. Americans from all walks of life felt strum those mystic chords of memory that bind us together as a proud people.

Tragedy and heroism are with us still, every day, in measures grand and mundane. Solidarity, though, feels in short supply. We as Americans must restore our unity by reminding ourselves that we, all of us, are in a covenant to defend one another’s natural rights. 

These self-evident truths about equality and freedom are set forth in our opening statement as a people, the Declaration of Independence.

Every one of us has a set of intrinsic rights:

• to survive;
• to not be tyrannized;
• to live the life we choose for ourselves;
• and to take part in determining who represents us and in holding them accountable.

That’s the American Promise, our mutual pledge to uphold these inalienable rights.

And the American Experiment is a project to protect one another’s rights by governing ourselves.

We are a people united by our commitment to uphold and defend this Experiment, lest it perish from the Earth.

These are the ideals Frederick Douglass championed in every speech he gave. This is the Founding Fathers in Philadelphia, Lincoln at Gettysburg, and Martin Luther King Jr. on the National Mall.

Americans fought for these ideals at Valley Forge, Shiloh and Normandy; we advanced them at Seneca Falls, Selma and Stonewall. The American Experiment is what the enemies on 9/11 so despised, and also why we felt so stubbornly proud that day, amidst the tremendous sorrow and suffering. 

We honor the heroes and victims of September 11 – and we re-animate our shared spirit as a people – when we recommit ourselves to our American Promise, our covenant to defend one another’s natural rights.”

Last November, I was one of 85 House Democrats to vote to condemn socialism. Democrats can be the party of Social Security and small business, of a strong floor and no ceiling. We should support free minds and free enterprise, whether threatened by government or corporate power. 

This fall, House Republicans are again resolving to 'denounce socialism in all its forms'. I voted no, as their resolution also 'calls for the enactment of the SAVE America Act', a Trump obsession that would nationalize elections and hand over voter rolls to Homeland Security – exactly the 'concentration of power' that the DC resolution warns can 'collapse into... dictatorships.'

To unlock the money for states and to dial down the distractions for children, Congress must pass my Parents Over Platforms Act. This bipartisan, bicameral bill establishes age assurance at the firmware level while protecting privacy. Without that protocol, the money and the measures that Meta has promised will melt away.

https://t.co/nM2Q9gjXAL
The Dignity Act: Give immigrants a pathway to legal certainty and freedom from fear. Secure the border. Fix the visa & asylum & E-Verify systems. https://t.co/k11c8pe7Wh
To help make real the American Creed, tax inheritance for billionaire heirs. https://t.co/YHffwUF5eT
AI agents should be liable for torts, just like humans are. Current law is sketchy. My bipartisan bill makes it clear. https://t.co/xmItji7myS
Tariffs must be stable, not slapdash. https://t.co/vRRUsyOYR8
This war was illegal, expensive, and optional. https://t.co/986SG7nI54
Sometimes politics is about turning private knowledge into common knowledge. https://t.co/elQ2ejSy2C
Meeting with entrepreneurs always gives me energy — and Nathaniel is an entrepreneur with lots of energy! https://t.co/LaZcxCeBXT
The war is already a failure. It must not become a quagmire. https://t.co/D0OuuTYZw9

Trump lost the kinetic war against Iran this year for the same reason he lost the trade war against China last year: chokepoint control. Iran closed off the Strait; China closed off critical minerals. Strategy in a networked world requires control over the essential nodes. America can't bomb its way to that control, much as Trump tries.

Two failures cause forever wars — sunk cost bias and groupthink. The Trump administration is making both mistakes. https://t.co/VqU6eWCUgR
